correctness.rationale: For the Thue–Morse fixed point mu(0)=01,mu(1)=10, any length-18 factor occurs in some mu^5(ab), a,b in {0,1}, because consecutive substitution blocks cover all four adjacent pairs; complete base enumeration yields 52 factors and exactly four 2-element fibres under twice removing first 1 and appending 1. Every nontrivial longer fibre projects to one of these four prefix pairs, so fibres remain disjoint pairs of forms {01z,10z} or {0110y,1001y}. A length>=5 left-special factor has a doubled letter (forbidden 01010,10101) fixing substitution parity; left specialness forces aligned even starts and lifts both preceding contexts. Desubstituting a left-special y of length>=14 and re-substituting yields both 0110y,1001y; the converse follows from common suffix contexts. Thus extra second-pass fibres biject with left-special factors of length n-4, yielding D2(n)=D1(n)+D1(n-2) for every n>=18. The n=17 counterexample D2(17)=5 versus 4 shows threshold sharp. Independent full-prefix factor enumeration verified n=17 and 103 lengths 18..120; infinite statement follows from parity/desubstitution, not checks.
